handoff: Review #1: one blocking finding. The story close y/N confirm runs inside withStory, under the tick lock, so every tick and watch fails tick_locked until the person answers. AC1–AC9 tested, suite and typecheck green. Minor: stale cmd.take hints (deferred to slice 14), confirm's for-await over stdin, a corrupt pushed story.md treated as open.

findings.title: The close prompt waits for the person under the tick lock
findings.detail:
`terminal.confirm(...)` runs inside the `withStory` callback, and `withStory` (`runtime/release.ts:15-25`) holds `acquireTickLock` for the whole callback. A person who leaves the prompt open, or walks away, blocks every `tick` and `watch` on this repo, which then fail `tick_locked` (exit 5) for as long as the prompt stays open. Nothing about consent needs the lock.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Ask before taking the lock: count the worktrees outside `withStory` (an observe or a view read without the lock), confirm, then enter `withStory` and run the B38 claim check again there. Add a test: while the fake interaction holds the confirm open, `tick` on the same root is not refused tick_locked (or assert that the lock is free while confirm runs).

findings.title: Printed hints still name `norn take`, which now exits 2
findings.detail:
`cmd.take` is still used in do_instead and printed commands: `runtime/human.ts:234,242,250,261,273`, `commands/workflow.ts:31,53`, `commands/open.ts:25`, `commands/update.ts:36`, `runtime/act/lifecycle.ts:195`. There is prose too: `view/src/orient.ts:170` and `README.md:55`, plus the lock note 'norn release' at `runtime/release.ts:104`. B7: 'copying a printed command always works'. The slice Notes defer this to slice 14 ('renamed in slice 14 if not already here'), so it does not block, but `cmd.take` → `cmd.storyCheckout` is a one-line swap at each call site.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Point the `cmd.take` users at `cmd.storyCheckout` and delete `cmd.take`, or confirm that slice 14 covers each of these sites.

findings.title: confirm returns from inside `for await` over process.stdin
findings.detail:
Leaving a `for await` early calls the async iterator's `return()`, which destroys `process.stdin`. Any later stdin read in the same process then fails. This is harmless today, since the process exits after the command. No newline is written to stderr after the answer.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Read one line with `once(stdin, 'data')` (or readline), then pause.

findings.title: An unreadable pushed story.md is treated as open
findings.detail:
When `parseStoryFile` fails, `isClosed` returns false without saying so. S2 says never guess. The local patch usually catches it later as story_corrupt, but not when no story worktree exists here.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Refuse it as `story_corrupt`, naming the ref and path.

findings.title: The claim_held refusal is written out twice, with a different exit code than checkout
findings.detail:
The same `${key} is held by … since …` text is built at `:32` and `:43`. Close exits 3 with code claim_held, while checkout's `claimHeld` exits 5 (busy) with the same code. B38 asks for exit 3, so the code is right, but one helper would keep the two in step.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Extract one helper for the close refusal.

findings.title: Small smells
findings.detail:
Divergent Change: the generic `withStory` now lives in the T6 release module. Duplicated Code: `story-checkout.ts:19-25` repeats the acquire-lock / busyError / finally-release shape. Mysterious Name: `aStory` in `runtime/target.ts:69`. `isClosed` uses both `ctx.git` and `(await ctx.ports()).git`.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Optional tidy-ups.
